<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0ab4a09e6525823c4b4b8dfa989f394b0a68b716` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a0c6890b3d9ae80d46fe7abfc49004df5c192d2a` — the merge of head `88387b3311c7510472e8794636ca541f4d09fb0e` into base `0ab4a09e6525823c4b4b8dfa989f394b0a68b716`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a0c6890b3d9ae80d46fe7abfc49004df5c192d2a && git checkout a0c6890b3d9ae80d46fe7abfc49004df5c192d2a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0ab4a09e6525823c4b4b8dfa989f394b0a68b716 88387b3311c7510472e8794636ca541f4d09fb0e && git checkout -B drift-repro 0ab4a09e6525823c4b4b8dfa989f394b0a68b716 && git merge --no-ff 88387b3311c7510472e8794636ca541f4d09fb0e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0ab4a09e6525823c4b4b8dfa989f394b0a68b716
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0ab4a09e6525823c4b4b8dfa989f394b0a68b716` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `04ba73c2207187c08cb3566eab228eab9658976d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-credential-carry-forward.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-clone.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/saveAdvisoryToast.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, .changeset/28640-withheld-not-carried-forward.md

Inputs read: card #28640 (body and all six comments, ruling 6566912252 and os-dev-report 6581427705 included), PR #29456 (body, 12-file list, net diff against the merge-base with `origin/main`, commit 7f277a86 of this repository), the check-runs on the head, the seat's delta (`/mnt/project-files/spec-seat2/28640-delta.md`), and the cited code in the live tree at the head via `git show`. Card slice: ②B only (①A is #29341, ③A's export marker is #29342). The rest of the diff (the four test files, the changeset, the regenerated `protocol.mdx`, the three `metadata-protocol` source files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the `metadata-protocol` files were READ here as the first consumer, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-02T16:02Z: 52 success, 8 skipped, 0 failure, 3 still in progress. Concluded green among the required set: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (all 16 shards), `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, and `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8 of 8; `Lint UI` skipped (no `ui/` path in the diff); `Check Changeset` success. Still running when this record was written: `Test Core` shards 3 and 5, and `Type Check · workspace`. No gate is red; the landing waits for those three to conclude green, as the queue rule already requires — this record judges the tree, and nothing below depends on their outcome.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`MetadataRedactionResult.notCarriedForwardKeys?: string[]`** (`@objectstack/spec/kernel`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts`) — a new OPTIONAL member on an exported interface. Public-surface WIDENING. **Right.** Every existing implementer type-checks unchanged (the `datasource` built-in and the derivation in this package, `redactFlowCredentials` in `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-projection.ts`; the PR's `legacyShape` test pins the type), and `absent means []` is honoured by the one reader (`planCarryForward`: `served.notCarriedForwardKeys ?? []`). `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json` lists the interface by name only, so no snapshot regeneration is owed (`check:api-surface` ran green on the head).
2. **Subset, not disjoint** — every not-carried-forward path is also in `redactedKeys`. **Right**, and the dev's fail-open claim measured TRUE at FOUR sites, not three: (a) `redactStoredMetadataBody` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts` L323) returns the RAW body when `result.redactedKeys.length === 0` — and `redactStoredMetadataRow(s)` above it, which the generic data door and the runtime reader contexts serve `sys_metadata` / `sys_metadata_history` through, inherit that; (b) `redactMetadataItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts` L140) returns the input; (c) `redactServedDocument` (`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts` L364) returns the record; (d) `planCarryForward` itself (`metadata-redaction.ts` L615) returns `none` on an empty `redactedKeys`, so with a disjoint list a row whose ONLY withheld position was an undeclared `auth` key would never reach the drop branch and never be reported. `packages/runtime/src/flow-clone.ts` L305 reads `redactedKeys` too, flow-only, unaffected either way. No reader in `ui/**` (`git grep redactedKeys` over `ui/**` at the head: zero hits). A disjoint list would have served that row in cleartext at (a)–(c) and silenced the drop at (d); the subset keeps all four correct with no edit. Deviation (1) is the right call.
3. **The connector redactor marks undeclared `auth` keys in both lists** (`redactConnectorItem`, item 1). For a non-cleared value the read exit's output is byte-identical to `main`'s; only the result gains the member. **Right.**
4. **A CLEARED undeclared `auth` key (`null`, `''`, `{}`) is now withheld** where `main` served it as written (merge-base `credentialPathsOf` pushed `auth.KEY` and the loop skipped `isClearedForm`). A read-side reduction of the served item. **Right**: the save door validates a connector against `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts` L272), whose instance-auth kinds are strict shapes since #28596, so on `main` a plain read-then-save of such a row was a 422 `unrecognized_keys` and the row could never drain; the PR's test pins `safeParse(item).success === false` for all three cleared forms and `true` for the served form. No accept set changes: the door refused the key before and refuses it still. Clients that read the cleared key: none found — `ui/**` has no reader of `auth.token` / undeclared auth keys (grep over `ui/packages/**` non-test sources: zero hits); a package export of the served form drops a key no import accepted. Deviation (2) is right.
5. **`SaveMetaItemResponseSchema.advisories` can now carry rule `withheld-key-dropped`, on a DRAFT save too** (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, description only; `rule` is an open `z.string()`, so no enum widens). **Right.** A client ignoring the key behaves as before; the key is still omitted when nothing is reported (the convergence test pins `not.toHaveProperty('advisories')` on the second save; the datasource CONTROL pins no key). New observable: a draft save, never gated (D1 early return), can now answer `advisories` — a client that assumed "draft saves carry no advisories" was reading an absence, not a contract (the schema declared the key optional on every save). `ui`'s `readSaveAdvisories` requires all six keys as strings; the notice supplies `rule`, `severity`, `where`, `path`, `message`, `hint` — it passes the filter and `formatFinding` renders it.
6. **`redactedPathsCarriedForward` no longer names an undeclared `auth` path** (the runtime gate's `restoredCredentialPaths`). **Right** — no rule reads an undeclared key; the test pins `['apiKey', 'providerConfig.headers']`.
7. **`metadata-protocol` public surface: unchanged.** `carryForwardRedactedValuesReportingDrops`, `droppedWithheldKeyNotices` and `WITHHELD_KEY_DROPPED` are module exports consumed inside the package; `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` (L178–222) still exports only `carryForwardRedactedValues`, `hasMetadataRedactor`, `redactMetadataItem(s)` and the stored-row family from `metadata-redaction.js`. `carryForwardRedactedCredentials` is a private method. The package's only published change is the content of a 2xx answer. Deviation (3) — the two files beyond the claimed four — is right: the save door (`protocol.ts` L17176–L17190, L17307) is where the answer is assembled and `advisories` is the ruled channel ("don't invent a second one", the delta's own words); `protocol.zod.ts` is the schema face and a `hits` file in any case.
8. **The notice never carries the value.** `droppedWithheldKeyNotices` (`protocol-credential-carry-forward.ts` L76–L95) builds `where`, `path`, `message` and `hint` from the type, the item name and the dotted path alone — the stored value is never an input to it, so no save shape (draft included) can leak it. The active-save test also asserts `allStrings(res)` excludes the token.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28640-withheld-not-carried-forward.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, carrying both declaration lines; the PR body carries the same two.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

**Matches the diff.** The level follows the metadata protocol alone (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3): nothing an author can write changes — no key, value or type added; `auth.KEY` was refused at the door before this PR and is refused after — so `none` → `patch` on both packages is the rule, and `check-changeset-no-major --event` (the `Check Changeset` run on the head) concluded success. `yes (widening)` is right for a new optional member on an exported interface plus a new advisory rule id on an open string field. The `(narrowing)` arm is not owed: the two sibling PRs on this same redactor that made the read serve LESS while the door's accept set stood (#28764, #28997) declared `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the one that narrowed the accept set (#28596) declared `no (narrowing)` / `narrowed` — this PR is of the first class on its read side and widens a type on top, so `yes (widening)` is the honest line. `Skills-docs: none` holds: no skill under `skills/**` teaches the connector read redaction or the save's carry-forward (`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` L96 speaks of flow `http` nodes only). Regenerated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` matches the new description byte for byte in the diff; `check:generated` ran green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (os-dev-report 6581427705), each answered or escalated:

- **open_questions 1 — member name `notCarriedForwardKeys`** (alternatives `droppedOnSaveKeys`, `drainedKeys`). A NEW PUBLIC NAME on `@objectstack/spec/kernel`. Judged fit: it names the mechanism in the ruling's own words and pairs with `carryForwardRedactedValues` / `redactedPathsCarriedForward`; nothing in the tree contradicts it. **Escalated to the maintainer by the seat** — this record does not stand in for that approval.
- **open_questions 2 — rule id `withheld-key-dropped`** (alternative `carry-forward-dropped`). A NEW PUBLIC NAME on the wire (`advisories[].rule`, the key a client groups or suppresses by, stable across releases). Judged fit: kebab-case like the gate's rule ids; names what happened to the row at rest. **Escalated to the maintainer by the seat**, as above.
- **open_questions 3 — subset vs disjoint.** ANSWERED: subset. Four fail-open readers named in ① item 2; the delta's "in the new list, not in `redactedKeys`" would have served cleartext at three read exits. The ruling's words ("the redactor can mark a position") admit either; the tree admits only the subset without reader edits.
- **open_questions 4 — keep withholding cleared undeclared `auth` keys.** ANSWERED: keep. On `main` the served `auth.token: null` met the strict shape at the door (422), so the ruled drain was unreachable for exactly those rows; no client reads the cleared key (① item 4). Recorded here as an accepted deviation from the delta.
- **open_questions 5 — the two files beyond the claimed four.** ANSWERED: accept (① item 7). The seat's claim comment 6578360910 named four source files; the save-door hunks are the consumer half the ruling itself names ("spec + metadata-protocol"), and the description is on a `hits` path.
- **Deviation 4** (no MCP writes / assignee set) — process, outside the tree; the standing order was followed.
- **Deviation 5 — `main` moved 25 commits after the gate run; one touches `protocol.ts`.** Read from the diff alone: `git diff 7f277a86..origin/main -- packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is three hunks at L8778, L9012 and L9123 (+36/−17); the PR's four hunks sit at L353 (import list), L3736–L3745, L17164–L17190 and L17293–L17310 — no overlap, the nearest pair more than 7,000 lines apart. Conflict risk: low; the import hunk adds one name to an existing block `main` did not touch. The queue leg re-judges on the merged base, as it must. No other file of the PR moved on `main` in the window.
- **Out-of-scope finding (dev, "noted, not filed")** — `sys_metadata_history` snapshots keep the pre-drain body; a read of them is served through the stored-row seam and withholds it, so there is no cleartext EXIT, only cleartext AT REST in history. Correctly outside ②B (the ruling's class is the live row's save). The dev marked it maintainer-reach; **the seat decides whether to file it as a follow-up card**, this record does not.
- **No `open_questions` entry was left unanswered.** Nothing in the report contradicts the tree.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts`** — judged against ruling ②B (6566912252) and its first consumer, `planCarryForward` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts` L603–L685). HOLDS. The docblock does what the delta asked: it says what a READ exit does with each list and what a SAVE's carry-forward does, and states the subset invariant and the "absent means `[]`" reading, both of which the consumer honours (`?? []`; the drop branch keyed off membership while iterating `redactedKeys`). Probes: (a) a redactor that names a path in `notCarriedForwardKeys` but NOT in `redactedKeys` — the consumer ignores it: the position was served, so the resent value is the author's word and is judged at the door. Fail-safe direction; the invariant is stated, not enforced, and no built-in violates it. Not a finding. (b) The connector sets the member only when non-empty — the CONTROL tests pin the member ABSENT on the datasource built-in, a derived (webhook) redactor and a connector with every other withheld position, so a reader using `toEqual` on those results is unchanged. (c) The module note's write-path paragraph now names the one fact a redactor states about the carry-forward; consistent with the consumer's header (`metadata-redaction.ts` L48–L57). No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts`** — judged against ruling ②B (the class is undeclared keys under `auth`), ③A (the four maps stay withheld WHOLE and carried forward — the CONTROL test pins `notCarriedForwardKeys` absent with all four maps plus `apiKey`, `authentication.key`, `retryConfig.secret`, `actions.0.token` and a credential URL withheld), and the strict instance-auth union (`packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts`: every static kind a strict shape with a required `credentialRef`). HOLDS. Probes: (a) order — items 7/8 first, then item 1, then the credential paths: `auth` is a declared root key, so item 7 never removes it and no path is pushed twice; item 1 reads `served` after items 7/8, correct. (b) Unknown `auth.type` — only `type` is declared, so every other key (a `credentialRef` included) is withheld AND not carried forward; the served `{ type: 'digest' }` then fails the union at the door (422), nothing is persisted and no notice is answered. Same outcome as `main` for an unsaveable row; the PR's test pins `notCarriedForwardKeys` equal to `redactedKeys` for it. Acceptable. (c) `auth` a non-object (item 4) — still carried forward, CONTROL pinned; the right boundary, since the whole value may be the secret and the ruling's class is keys UNDER `auth`. (d) A legacy row `{ type: 'bearer', token: X }` with no `credentialRef` — served `{ type: 'bearer' }`, save refused for the missing `credentialRef`; the author must supply the reference before the row drains. Correct: the kind asks for its reference again, and nothing is lost that the door would have accepted. (e) The "Cleared forms" paragraph of the module note is amended to name items 1, 7 and 8 as the exception — the note and the code agree. No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** — judged against the ruling's "the save result names the dropped keys in its notices" and the consumer that emits them (`droppedWithheldKeyNotices`, `protocol-credential-carry-forward.ts` L76–L95; the save door `protocol.ts` L17176–L17190 and L17307) and the two `ui/` readers. HOLDS. The description is the published contract text for a behaviour the consumer measurably has: one `warning` per dropped position, draft saves included, key omitted when empty. `path` spelling `connectors[0].auth.token` is the schema's own positional rule: `connectors` is not a name-keyed context collection (`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts` L587–L592: `objects`, `permissions`, `books`, `datasets` only), so the written item IS `[0]`; an index segment in the dotted path is re-spelled `[i]` (`actions.0.KEY` → `actions[0].KEY`), matching the gate's nested spelling. `where` follows the gate's `TYPE "name"` form. `hint` is REQUIRED by `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema` and `ui`'s `readSaveAdvisories` drops a finding without it — the notice supplies it. No `ui/**` mirror of `MetadataRedactionResult` exists, and the advisory shape is re-exported from `@objectstack/spec` (`RuntimeAuthoringIssue`) rather than restated (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts` L49–L71), so there is no objectui#7715-class mirror to drop the new member or rule. No must-fix.

Should-fix (one, low): the notice's `message` says "the stored row held a value at 'auth.token' … this save removed it from the row at rest". Two cases make that sentence imprecise: a cleared form (`token: null` is reported with the same words — the row held a cleared position, not "a value"), and the code-layer fallback (`storedBodyForCarryForward` compares against the CODE layer when no overlay row exists, so the first save creates an overlay WITHOUT the key and removes nothing from any row). Both are wording, not behaviour: the drop, the convergence and the loudness are right in each case. Remedy: say "held a position at …, which the read withholds and no save keeps; this save stored the row without it" — one string in `droppedWithheldKeyNotices`, and the two `droppedNotice` expectations use `objectContaining` without `message`, so no test moves. May land as a follow-up.

Observations, not findings: (i) the `ui` toast title (`saveAdvisoryToast.ts` L122) frames every advisory as "the authoring check raised N advisory finding(s)"; a drop notice is the save's own, not the gate's — a `ui/` wording follow-up, and the channel is the ruled one. (ii) The draft-save test asserts the notice shape but not `allStrings(res)` against the token; the emitter is value-blind by construction (① item 8) and the active-save test asserts it, so the pin is adequate. (iii) The publish door (`protocol.ts` L18750) runs no carry-forward and promotes the draft body; a draft saved through the save door is already drained, and a pre-PR draft still holding the key drains on its next save — consistent with the ruling's "a normal save".

## 待裁：两个新公开名字 `notCarriedForwardKeys` 与 `withheld-key-dropped`（#28640 ②B）

- 一句话问题：连接器的认证配置里如果残留一个未声明的密钥（例如旧版的 `auth.token`），读出时它被隐藏，再保存时却会被原样带回，永远清不掉。这个 PR 让保存时丢掉这类键并告诉作者，为此新增两个公开名字，需要您定。
- 背景：总监裁定 ②B（6566912252）：未声明的认证键读出隐藏、保存不带回、并给作者一条提示。席位的契约复审判 PASS（6581889597）。
- 名字一：`MetadataRedactionResult.notCarriedForwardKeys`（`@objectstack/spec/kernel` 接口上的可选成员，是 `redactedKeys` 的子集：隐藏且保存时不带回的路径）。
  - A 保留：与现有的 `carryForwardRedactedValues`、`redactedPathsCarriedForward` 同一套"带回"用语，零额外工作。
  - B 改名（`droppedOnSaveKeys` 或 `drainedKeys`）：更直说"保存时丢掉"，但与"带回"那组名字不成对；改名约半小时（改代码、测试、重新生成参考页），复审补 delta。
- 名字二：保存提示的规则 id `withheld-key-dropped`（出现在保存响应 `advisories[].rule`，客户端按它归类或屏蔽，发布后应保持稳定）。
  - A 保留：与现有规则 id 一样用短横线，直说"被隐藏的键被丢掉"。
  - B 改为 `carry-forward-dropped`：强调"带回机制丢掉了它"，与名字一的用语更贴近；改名成本同上。
